title: Optimal local recovery cannot alter critical orthogonality exponents in quantum spin environments
abstract: We prove a local amplitude-ratio bound for positive ground states and an explicit reverse comparison for fidelity under finite-region erasure. An exact lattice calculation for a connected critical Ising chain gives amplitude exponent $1/8$, preserved by arbitrary optimal control on any fixed spin set and, at the level of logarithmic exponents, on $o(\log N)$ spins. We derive the finite Cauchy product and its uniform strip asymptotics, and document exact two-spin optimization and an interferometric protocol for measuring the recovery. A separate finite-mediator theorem quantifies local compression and a decoder while retaining the rest of the environment exactly. We also give a ground-preparation Ramsey bound, counterexamples to stronger projected-state inferences, and independent full-Hamiltonian calculations.
summary: This theoretical paper establishes fundamental bounds on how much quantum interference information can be recovered when only local measurements or controls are available. By analyzing critical quantum spin chains, the authors prove that the inherent critical orthogonality exponent remains invariant under optimal local recovery protocols. This work sets rigorous limits on the information extractable from a system when global control is impossible.
main_problem: The paper investigates the fundamental limit of interference recovery (quantum erasure) when only local control is available over a quantum system, specifically determining if optimal local recovery can alter critical orthogonality exponents.
main_result: The authors prove that optimal local recovery cannot alter the critical orthogonality exponent, demonstrating that this exponent governs the collective limit of interference loss even when local control is applied.
method: The analysis employs rigorous mathematical bounds, including local amplitude-ratio bounds, comparison of full vs. recovered fidelity ($F_{	ext{full}}$ vs $F_R$), and techniques involving imaginary-time evolution and Cauchy product asymptotics.
model_or_system: The study focuses on quantum spin environments, exemplified by a connected critical Ising chain. The system is described by Hamiltonians involving local bias terms and is analyzed in the context of finite-region erasure.
key_observables: Orthogonality exponent, fidelity ($F_{	ext{full}}$, $F_R$), recovery gain ($\Lambda_M$), and local component ratios.
important_parameters: The critical exponent (e.g., $1/8$ for the Ising chain), the size of the controlled region ($|M|$), and local energy scales ($\Lambda_M$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes positive ground-state Hamiltonians and uniformly bounded ratios of local longitudinal bias to transverse field, and requires no gap in the environment.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares the bare overlap and optimized amplitude for a sign-defect chain, showing the preservation of the critical exponent. Figure 2 illustrates recoverable local records at finite mediator energy.
paper_structure: The paper develops bounds by comparing full state overlaps to locally recovered states, deriving local amplitude-ratio bounds, and applying these to specific models like the Ising chain to prove the invariance of critical exponents.
why_interesting: This work provides deep insights into the robustness of critical quantum phenomena against local perturbations, which is crucial for understanding quantum error correction and the limits of measurement in complex quantum many-body systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Optimal local recovery preserves a critical orthog- onality exponent. For the connected sign-defect chain, the erased spins are the two adjacent to the central bond, M = {L, L + 1}. (a) Bare overlap FN and optimal amplitude FR, computed from the physical two-spin transition matrix. The dashed reference has exponent 1/8, established analytically in Eq. (11). (b) Their ratio approaches a finite enhancement in the displayed data. All 15 sizes from N = 16 to 2048 are shown; at the largest size FR/FN = 1.13278. Equation (12) bounds the ratio by 5 for every size, independently of this numerical trend.

FIG. 2. A recoverable local record at finite mediator energy. Complete ground states of a periodic four-cell (12-spin) pen- dant chain give the bare transition weight Zfull = F 2 full and optimal leaf-only weight ZR = F 2 R. Parameters are K = 1, h = 40, j = 20, ϵ = 0.01, and a = 1.25001500016. At g/h = 1.2, Zfull = 0.04379 whereas ZR = 0.98099. The dashed curve, W 4 ϵ , is the squared overlap contributed by the four driven leaves in their conditional ground states, derived in the Supplemental Material. All displayed weights refer to this finite system.
